reason: E1 shows Mn segregation at GBs during 700°C tensile testing but explicitly states that the concentration is insufficient and the time too short to form precipitates, contradicting the claim that segregation promotes precipitate nucleation. E2 shows that brittle precipitates can form in nanocrystalline HEA at 450°C, but this is a different grain-size regime and does not support the premise for the proposed coarse-grained, single-phase condition. The cited evidence therefore does not support the key mechanistic link from segregation to precipitate formation under the stated conditions.
premises: Mn segregates to grain boundaries in CrMnFeCoNi under thermal and mechanical driving forces
Mn segregation promotes nucleation of brittle intergranular precipitates (e.g., L10-NiMn or Cr-rich sigma)
Formation of these precipitates degrades toughness
A variant with reduced Mn or inhibited segregation will retain toughness under the same conditions
